data.narrative:
Krevera is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Edward and Sebastian Schneeweiss that has raised $3M+. The valuation assessment draws from a sector universe comprising 1 public comparable (277810.KQ) and 8 private peers including Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Bedrock Robotics.

The stage-progression method is applicable and forms the primary analytical anchor. Using the $3M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a typical 2.5x step-up multiplier from seed to the subsequent funding stage yields an implied valuation of $8M. The peer-median method, while standard practice, cannot be reliably applied here due to insufficient data density; only one same-stage peer was identified within the narrow robotics and manufacturing cohort, falling well short of the three-datapoint threshold needed for robust triangulation. Relying on the broader sector median would risk obscuring stage-specific and company-specific factors material to valuation.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $6M to $9M, with a median of $8M. This range reflects a ±15% band around the stage-progression result. Key uncertainties include the absence of direct peer valuation multiples in the robotics & manufacturing seed stage and the limited visibility into Krevera's unit economics, revenue trajectory, or technological differentiation relative to the identified peer set. A subsequent funding event or narrowing of the peer cohort would improve estimate precision.
